stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav's brother Prateek passes away:Cardiac arrest after blood clot in lungs, SP MLA demands probe into ‘suspicious’ death
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav’s younger brother Prateek Yadav died on Wednesday. He was 38 years old. In the morning, around 6 am, his brother-in-law Aman Singh Bisht, brother of wife Aparna Yadav, took him to Lucknow Civil Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. According to Civil Hospital Chief Medical Superintendent Dr DC Pandey, Prateek’s pulse had completely stopped when he was brought to the hospital. His heart had also stopped beating. A post-mortem of Prateek Yadav’s body was conducted at Lucknow Medical College. According to the report, he died due to cardiac arrest. Six old injury marks were found on the body. Viscera samples have been preserved. Prateek’s body has been kept at his residence for people to pay their last respects. His last rites will be performed on Thursday at 11 am at Baikunth Dham in Lucknow. When Prateek died, his wife and BJP leader Aparna Yadav were in Assam. She has now returned to Lucknow. Aparna had gone to Assam on Tuesday for the oath-taking ceremony of Himanta Biswa Sarma. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Minister Suresh Khanna, Dimple Yadav and Shivpal Yadav, along with several senior leaders, reached the residence. Akhilesh Yadav visited the post-mortem house in the morning and later reached Prateek Yadav’s residence in the afternoon. He appeared emotional while paying tribute. Samajwadi Party MLA Ravidas Mehrotra said Prateek’s death happened under suspicious circumstances. He claimed there were injury marks on the body and demanded an inquiry by a former High Court judge. Prateek’s wife, BJP leader Aparna Yadav, returned to Lucknow immediately from Assam, where she had been attending the swearing-in ceremony of Himanta Biswa Sarma. Several prominent figures have visited the family home to pay their respects, including, Yogi Adityanath, Suresh Khanna, Dimple Yadav and Shivpal Yadav. Akhilesh calls stepbrother Prateek’s death “extremely saddening” Deputy CM Keshav Maurya expresses grief over Prateek’s death According to sources, Prateek was admitted to a private hospital in Lucknow in critical condition on April 30. He showed slight improvement after three days, following which he reportedly returned home without formal discharge. Doctors said he was suffering from pulmonary embolism, a serious lung condition in which a blood clot gets stuck in the arteries of the lungs and blocks blood circulation. Prateek was the son of Sadhna Gupta, the second wife of Mulayam Singh Yadav. Sadhna Gupta was first married to Chandraprakash Gupta in 1986, and Prateek was born in 1987. The couple divorced in 1990. Around the same time, Sadhna grew close to Mulayam Singh Yadav. In 2003, Mulayam Singh married Sadhna Gupta and publicly acknowledged Prateek as his son. Pictures related to Prateek’s death Studied in Britain, stayed away from politics Prateek studied at the University of Leeds in Britain and remained away from active politics. He was involved in the real estate and fitness business and owned a gym in Lucknow called ‘The Fitness Planet’. Prateek had married Aparna Yadav in a love marriage 14 years ago. The couple has two daughters. On January 19, Prateek had unexpectedly announced his decision to divorce Aparna, saying that she had made his life “hell”. However, nine days later, the two reconciled. Prateek later shared a picture with Aparna on Instagram and wrote, “All is Good.”

stories.title: CM Shubhendu PA murder case:Third accused arrested from Varanasi; Ghazipur resident among 3 held in UP so far
stories.summary: CBI has arrested an accused from Varanasi in the murder of Chandranath Rath, PA to West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. Vinay Rai Pampam (40) is a resident of Deoria village in Ghazipur. CBI produced him in the CGM Court. After this, CBI left for Bengal with Vinay Rai. On Monday, a CBI team had also arrested Rajkumar Singh, a resident of Ballia, from Muzaffarnagar. He is considered the main shooter in the murder case. Earlier, on May 10, Raj Singh, also a resident of Ballia, was arrested from Ayodhya. Thus, 3 accused have been arrested from UP so far. Chandranath Rath, 42, was shot dead on May 6, two days after the results of the Bengal elections were announced. The attackers stopped his car and fired several rounds. Chandranath Rath sustained 3 bullet wounds to his chest and abdomen. Due to the seriousness of the case, the investigation was handed over to the CBI. Vinay has been imprisoned in Tihar Jail Vinay Rai, a resident of Deoria village, has a criminal history. Several serious cases, including murder, attempted murder, and the Gangster Act, are registered against him. His name also surfaced in the 2017 murder of Nanhku Yadav and the shooting of Arvind Yadav. Vinay has also been to Tihar Jail after his arrest with illegal weapons from the Delhi-Haryana border in 2012. Now know who is Rajkumar, whom the CBI arrested on May 18 Tribhuvan Narayan Singh, a resident of Ballia, used to work for LT in Ayodhya. He has been at home since retiring in March. He has 2 sons and one daughter. The daughter is the eldest. The youngest son studies in class 5. Rajkumar Singh is Tribhuvan's elder son. He studied up to BA first year. He dropped out of studies because he wasn't interested. After that, he started working as a crane helper in Mumbai. However, he left the job 8 months ago and came home. Rajkumar was preparing to go abroad for work, after getting his passport made. About 3 years ago, he had been to jail after his name came up in a dispute with people from the Harijan community in Rattopur village of Ballia. The first accused, Raj Singh, was arrested on May 10 Raj Singh, a resident of Ballia, was arrested from Ayodhya on May 10 in connection with the murder of PA Chandranath Rath. He was then sent to 13 days of police custody by the court. After his arrest, a poster of Raj Singh surfaced. In it, he has identified himself as the State General Secretary of Akhil Bharatiya Kshatriya Mahasabha. His Facebook account has a picture with Minister Dayashankar Singh. He also has a reel with former MP Brijbhushan Singh. According to neighbors, Raj wanted to become a politician. He was preparing to contest the Block Pramukh election. Suspicion of 8 people being involved in the murder Investigating agencies believe that at least 8 people were involved in the conspiracy and execution of the murder. These individuals had conducted reconnaissance for several days before killing PA Chandranath Rath. The attackers' car had passed through the Bali Toll Plaza before the murder. Here, a person in the car had paid the toll via UPI. Through the mobile number linked to this digital transaction, the police identified one accused. Then they reached the rest of the accused. Meanwhile, after initial investigation, Bengal Police had suspected the involvement of contract killers in Chandranath Rath's murder. Police had stated that Rath's murder was planned. Professional shooters might be involved in it. Police had seized a car from the crime scene, which was used to chase Rath's Scorpio. The car's number plate turned out to be fake. The car's chassis and engine numbers were erased. Additionally, 2 bikes were involved in the attack. One of these bikes was also found near a tea shop about 4 km from the crime scene. It also had a fake registration. Chandranath was with Suvendu since he was in TMC Chandranath was previously an officer in the Air Force. After taking VRS, he worked in the corporate sector for some time. After that, he entered politics. Chandranath had been working for Suvendu since he was in the Trinamool Congress. He was considered among Suvendu Adhikari's very close associates. Chandranath became part of Suvendu's official team in 2019, when Suvendu was a minister in the Mamata Banerjee government. Chandranath had taken charge of Suvendu's election campaign in Bhawanipur. Bhawanipur is the same seat from where Suvendu defeated Mamata Banerjee by about 15 thousand votes in the assembly elections. Chandranath's mother also joined BJP with Suvendu Like Suvendu, Chandranath's family was also earlier associated with TMC. His mother, Hashi Rath, held a position in the local panchayat body in Purba Medinipur during TMC rule, but joined BJP with Suvendu Adhikari in 2020. Chandranath was calm and low-profile. He completed his education from Rahara Ramakrishna Mission. Despite being close to Suvendu for many years, he always stayed away from the limelight. There is no photo of Chandrakant with Suvendu. Understand the entire incident with a 90-minute timeline Chandranath left Kolkata around 9 o'clock: Chandranath was returning from Kolkata in a Scorpio to go to his rented house in Madhyamgram. The driver was driving the car. Chandranath was sitting next to him. Scorpio seen in CCTV at 10 PM: Chandranath's Scorpio was seen passing on the road in a CCTV camera at 9:58 PM in Madhyamgram, about 20 kilometers from Kolkata. A short while after the Scorpio passed, a car and three people on two bikes were seen following from the area. 10:30 AM: Car blocked Scorpio's path: Near Doharia Junction in Madhyamgram, the car overtook the Scorpio and stopped in front of it. The Scorpio driver had to stop the car. Attackers on a bike started firing: Before Chandranath and his driver could understand anything, the bike-borne attackers came from the left and fired 6 to 10 rounds. Miscreants fled leaving the car: After committing the crime, the miscreants left the car there and fled on motorcycles via two different routes. Car's number plate fake: Police seized the car from the crime scene, but when the number was checked, it turned out to be fake. The car's chassis number had also been tampered with. Glock 47X pistol used in murder: The attackers used a Glock 47X pistol. Such modern weapons are not used by ordinary criminals. The way the attack happened, only a professional shooter could have carried it out.

Saying this, ITBP jawan Vikas Singh broke down. On Monday, Vikas had reached Police Commissioner Raghuvir Lal. When he showed the Commissioner his mother's severed hand, he was stunned. Vikas said that his mother had a stomach problem. Due to wrong treatment at Krishna Hospital located at Tatmil Chauraha, her hand turned black. After infection, the hand had to be amputated. The Commissioner had the severed hand placed in a thermocol box. He spoke to the CMO about the matter and asked for an investigation. Raghuvir Lal also assured that an FIR would be registered after the investigation. Only then did Constable Vikas Singh's tears stop. ITBP officers also arrived with the constable. stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Rahul Gandhi begins 2-day UP visit, slams PM Modi; fuel costs go up for 2nd time in 5 days more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day- 1. Fuel costs go up for 2nd time in 5 days; Petrol, diesel prices up 90 paisa across India Petrol and diesel prices on Tuesday increased by around 90 paise per litre across the country, the second hike in less than a week. 2. Rahul Gandhi alleges Modi left for foreign tour instead of handling situation in country Congress MP Rahul Gandhi is on a two-day visit to Uttar Pradesh. Speaking in Rae Bareli on Tuesday, he said an economic storm is about to hit the country. He alleged that the economic structure created by Prime Minister Narendra Modi for Adani and Ambani will not survive and will completely collapse. He added that ordinary people will suffer the most because of it. 3. Suvendu's PA murder accused Rajkumar has criminal record The main shooter Rajkumar Singh, arrested in the murder of Chandranath Rath, PA to West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, had previously been jailed in an assault case. A case under the SC/ST Act is ongoing against him. Currently, he was out on bail. During the investigation, a photo of shooter Rajkumar with Bhojpuri actor Pawan Singh also surfaced, in which he is seen standing with Pawan in a green T-shirt. 4. SC says ‘Dangerous dogs should be given lethal injections' The Supreme Court of India has ruled that dangerous or rabies-infected stray dogs may be euthanised through injection, stating that the protection of human life is paramount and that the right to live with dignity includes freedom from the threat posed by stray dogs. 5. SP faces backlash after controversial Brahmin-prostitute comment Date May 5. Jawahar Bhawan in Delhi. It was the launch event of a book titled 'Viruses of Caste and Communalism'. SP's national spokesperson Rajkumar Bhati made a comment about Brahmins. He said - 'Neither a Brahmin is good, nor a prostitute is good...'. A controversy was bound to erupt over his statement, and that's exactly what happened. 6. Cooling pads installed at Zoo to protect snakes from heat The effect of heat has started showing on the reptiles of Kanpur Zoo as well. Cold-blooded creatures like snakes and iguanas are also troubled by this scorching heat. To protect snakes from this heat, Kanpur Zoo administration has come up with a unique and indigenous solution. 7. Iran plans ₹500 crore bounty on Trump, Netanyahu assassins Iran's parliament is likely to introduce a bill to reward more than ₹500 crore for those who assassinated US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. 8. Bijnor teen converts in Kashmir, recite Kalma in mosque, police launch probe A 17-year-old boy from Bijnor was allegedly converted to Islam in Jammu and Kashmir, with the family learning about it only two days ago after the boy called them and shared pictures claiming he had accepted Islam. 9. IMD issues heatwave warning for 39 UP districts: Banda hottest in the country with 47.6°C Severe heat and heatwave continue to prevail in UP. The mercury has crossed 47 °C. Banda remained the hottest city in the country for the second consecutive day. The maximum temperature was recorded at 47.6 °C. Since Tuesday morning, people in all districts have been suffering due to the intense sunlight. Loo-like winds are blowing. 10. ‘World sees a compromised PM in panic’, Rahul slams PM Modi over Norwegian journalist row Rahul Gandhi criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi for not answering a female journalist’s question during his visit to Norway. Sharing a post by Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng on X, Rahul wrote, “What happens to India's image when the world sees a compromised PM panic and run from a few question?"

stories.title: MP Iqra Hasan alleges police detention after clash with inspector:Warns officials, ‘don’t touch me’; ex-minister among 4 arrested
stories.summary: In Saharanpur on Tuesday afternoon, an argument broke out between SP MP Iqra Hasan from Kairana and police personnel. When a woman inspector asked her to come to the police station, Iqra Hasan said in a stern tone - Don't you dare touch me. Iqra alleges that the police took her into custody. She was made to sit in the women's police station for about 10 minutes. When the inspector offered her water at the station, the MP said, I don't want to drink your water. Following the news of Iqra being taken into custody, many of her supporters also arrived. Later, the MP was released. However, four people including former Minister of State and SP leader Mangeram Kashyap have been arrested. All of them were taken to Sadar Bazaar police station for medical examination. Iqra said, instead of listening to the victim's complaint, the police is harassing them. When the MP was asked whether she would raise this matter in Parliament, she said, There is no point in speaking in the current government, because there is no hearing. See 3 pictures... Iqra Hasan had reached the DIG with an elderly woman Iqra Hasan said, I had gone to DIG Abhishek Singh with an elderly woman victim from Jasala village. The woman was demanding a fair investigation in the murder case of her son. The MP alleges that the DIG listened to me, but refused to accept the victim's demands. After this, he got up from his office and left. At this, the woman became emotional and left the office feeling hurt. Iqra Hasan said that the DIG did not give the woman a full opportunity to present her case. MP said - I did not obstruct traffic The MP protested in support of the woman. Iqra Hasan came out of the office to the parking area. She alleges that after this, police were called on the DIG's instructions on charges of blocking the road and she was taken into custody. According to the MP, the police took her to the women's police station saying she was obstructing traffic. She claimed that she has video evidence of this incident. No traffic was obstructed anywhere. Iqra Hasan alleged that she was made to sit in the women's police station for about 10 minutes. The MP called it an act of pressurizing and said that the administration should seriously listen to the problems of the victims. What happened at the police station, what did the MP say... understand the whole matter… Question- Did you come regarding the Jasala case that had happened? Iqra- Yes. Question- Okay, so what conversation took place there? Iqra- We came with the victims. (Just then a woman police officer arrives and asks them to go inside) Iqra says to the woman police officer- No, don't touch me. Woman Police Officer- No, I'm not touching, I'm asking you to walk this way. Iqra- Don't touch me. Woman Police Officer- I didn't touch you. Iqra- You just touched me. Woman Police Officer- Hey, I'm showing you the way. Iqra- You just touched me. Woman Police Officer- You're going that way. Iqra- You just touched me. (Just then the journalist asks the question again) Question: So what would you like to say madam, is dictatorship happening? Iqra- You are seeing it yourself. If an MP meets the DIG with a victim's family and the DIG tells the victim's family in front of them 'Go away, we will do what we have to do', then this is dictatorship. And then we were brought here to the women's police station. (While going inside the police station) Iqra- Come on, let's go ahead now. Why are you touching my hands? Now the scene at the women's police station (Iqra Hasan sits on a chair in the room and police personnel offer her water) Woman Police Officer- Water... Iqra- No, we don't want... We don't want to drink your water. Okay? No, we absolutely don't want to drink yours. Woman Police Officer- Do you people have any problem... Iqra- You people are not understanding the victim's suffering. Yes, there is a mother whose child has died, in this manner... and you will give us water? We don't want to drink your water, keep it with you. Woman Police Officer- Whatever happens, keeps happening. There's no problem with that. Iqra- Yes, fine. The problem is for her, the mother, why would you have any problem? Iqra- Tell us why we were brought here? We have other work too. Our work is not just to sit in the office, we have other work as well. Police Officer- No problem, you wait for 10 minutes, today somehow, we will inform you. Finally, conversation with journalists... Question- MP ji, could you please explain in detail what exactly happened? Iqra- Brother, we had gone to meet the DIG sahab. Regarding the action that took place in Jasala, the mother is continuously saying that she has not received justice. We had come to the DIG sahab with her plea for justice. Monu Kashyap's mother presented her side. The DIG sahab refused to listen to the mother's statement. He told that poor, oppressed, elderly mother to 'leave from here'. I had gone with her, I could not tolerate it and then the DIG sahab himself got up and left from there. So we came out, we were planning to create an application again, we were talking when the police pounced on us saying 'don't create a commotion here'. We were in the parking lot, we were not on the road. We also have the recording. The road kept running continuously. Now on the basis of the road, traffic, they have brought me here to the women's police station. So this is outright dictatorship and clearly the police are working only for these BJP people. Question- What do you think, have they brought you here regarding the traffic issue or something else? Iqra- You people were also there, traffic was continuously moving. We also have video recording available. There was no disruption in traffic, we were standing in the parking space and these same people had said to submit another application, we were talking about that there. So they called all the women police of the entire district there, to intimidate us, to put pressure on us. But we will not be scared, they can do whatever they want to do. These are my people, when they are in pain then I am in pain and I will stand with them. Question- Where have they kept you now? Iqra- Right now they have brought me to the women's police station in Saharanpur. Now know about that case, for which Ikra Hasan had gone to advocate... Monu Kashyap (25) from village Jasala in Kandhla police station area of Shamli was found injured near the railway line at Panjokhra on the night of April 21. Police took Monu to CHC, from where doctors referred him to Meerut. Monu died during treatment. After the incident, the family had expressed suspicion of murder. Monu's mother accused his friends Sachin and Shubham of murder. Police examined Monu's call details and mobile location. The investigation revealed that Sachin and Shubham were present with Monu at the time of the incident. Police arrested Sachin and Shubham on April 25. After the crime, the accused were hiding at different tube wells in the Kandhla area. At the time of arrest, both were planning to flee to Delhi. Both accused work as laborers and electrical fitters. There was a dispute over talking to his girlfriend It came to light during interrogation that Sachin and Shubham were close friends of Monu. Monu had two girlfriends. The accused wanted him to arrange their conversation with one of the young women, but Monu kept refusing. There had been several disputes between the three over this matter before. According to the police, the accused plotted the murder out of this grudge. On April 21, Sachin and Shubham called Monu near the railway track on the pretext of having a party. The three sat there and drank alcohol. During drinking, both accused again demanded to talk to the young woman. When Monu refused again, the dispute escalated. After this, both of them together started beating him. As soon as the train approached nearby, both pushed Monu in front of the train. Monu was seriously injured in the accident. Later, he died during treatment. SP City Vyom Bindal said, Information was received that some people had blocked the road outside the DIG office and caused a jam. Police promptly reached there. The road was made operational smoothly there. Appropriate legal action is being taken against those who were involved in this. Who is Iqra Hasan?

stories.title: Akhilesh asks ‘What’s wrong with praying on roads?’:Accuses BJP of deflecting from real issues; backs Congress alliance
stories.summary: 'There are rules about what should and shouldn't happen on roads. As far as roads are concerned, we want roads to be wider. They are raising this issue so that the debate shifts in another direction. Who is offering namaz on the roads? And even if someone is, if there's less space, what's the problem? They want us to get entangled in other matters. But we have also learned from BJP. We won't get caught up in their talk. We will first ask what happened to NEET, tell us that? We will ask about the 69,000 teachers and the reservation that has been snatched away.' This statement was made by SP chief Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday while countering CM Yogi's statement given yesterday. He was speaking at an event organized by media house ‘Amar Ujala’. In the same event, Yogi had said that if you want to offer namaz, do it at a designated place. If the numbers are more, then do it in shifts. Read what else Akhilesh said? We have always benefited others, not deceived them How many seats will you give to Congress in the assembly elections? On this question, Akhilesh said that even in the Lok Sabha, the question was not of seats, but of victory. The same formula will continue in the assembly as well. We will contest the 2027 assembly elections with an alliance. We have long experience of forming and running alliances. Socialists have always benefited others, never betrayed them. PM has refused to go abroad, we will definitely tour abroad Akhilesh Yadav said - The alliance will not be based on the number of seats. I will not reveal what our strategy will be in the assembly elections. Our opponent is very powerful. Akhilesh also took a jibe at the appeal to postpone the PM's foreign visit. He said that we are people of the opposition. The Prime Minister has refused to go abroad, but we will roam abroad. Akhilesh's taunt - If the Prime Minister had landed in Iran, there would have been no war Taking a jibe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Akhilesh said that the way he landed in Pakistan without permission, if he had landed in Iran, there would have been no war. If India's Prime Minister had stood with Iran, there would have been no war. Not today, but tomorrow or the day after, the world's experts will definitely agree with this. The gold you have accumulated over 10 years is the reason it has become expensive. All jewelers' shops will close down in one year. Lathis are being used on lawyers Akhilesh Yadav said on CM Yogi's statement that there should be no political scoring. Just yesterday, people from our Bar Association came out to protest. They were lathi-charged. They were beaten, even though they had Ramcharitra Manas in their hands. If they call themselves Sanatani, then there should be Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam (the world is one family). We embrace everyone. They couldn't build a Smart City, even smart meters had to be removed. So what should we say about the government?

stories.title: Bijnor teen allegedly converted in Kashmir:Made to recite Kalma in mosque; told family, 'My new name is Hamza'
stories.summary: A 17-year-old boy from Bijnor was allegedly converted to Islam in Jammu and Kashmir, with the family learning about it only two days ago after the boy called them and shared pictures claiming he had accepted Islam. The matter came to light after villagers found videos circulating on social media showing the teenager reciting the Kalma inside a mosque and embracing Islam. In the videos, it was claimed that his name had been changed to Hamza. According to the boy’s father, his behaviour had noticeably changed over the past few months. The father said the teenager later told the family over the phone, “I have gone very far from you now. I do not want to return to Hinduism. I have accepted Islam of my own free will. My new name is Hamza.” When questioned about the viral videos, the boy reportedly denied uploading them himself. The family has alleged that the conversion was forced and says they are in deep shock since the incident surfaced. They approached a former MP and local MLA for help, met the Superintendent of Police, and demanded that the boy be brought back. Police have registered a case and launched an investigation into the matter. The incident is reported from the Kotwali area, around five kilometres from the district headquarters. First, see these two pictures... First, understand the whole matter in a sequential manner- Went to Jammu and Kashmir three years ago, started working in a salon Krishna Kumar, a resident of Khanjahanpur Bahadur, works as a laborer. He said - his son had passed the high school examination three years ago. His age on the marksheet is 17 years and 4 months. He was acquainted with Waseem, son of Liaqat, a resident of Kajiwala. Waseem's brother took him to Kashmir three years ago. Behavior changed in recent months, stopped sending money He said - his son learned to work at a salon. Later, he opened a salon in partnership with Bilal Pathan in Kupwara. Everything went well for some time. He used to send money to the family. However, his behavior changed a lot in recent months. He often argued with family members over the phone. He also stopped sending money. Came to the village on May 5, returned to Kashmir two days later He said - The son came to his village on May 5. When the family asked him to get married, he agreed. On May 6, he also went to see the girl with his family. He liked the girl. On May 7, he went back to Kashmir. On May 8, he called home and refused to get married. Video received on uncle's mobile, showed him converting to Islam The father said - Two days ago, some people sent Instagram videos to my brother's mobile. The video showed the son converting to Islam. The family alleges that the video was uploaded on Instagram to put pressure on the son. Now, know what is visible in the video Two videos related to the boy's religious conversion have surfaced. The videos are from Markazi Jamia Masjid in Ganderbal district of Kashmir. In the first video, the cleric is seen making the boy recite the Kalma. They are giving him a new name, Mohammed Hamza. In the second video, the boy is seen coming out of the mosque. He has flower garlands around his neck. People walking with him are seen laughing. Family members complained to the SP On Monday, led by former BJP MP Bhartendu Singh, family members and villagers reached the SP's office. They demanded the safe return of the minor and strict action against the accused. Former MP Bhartendu Singh said, "The child is a minor. Religious conversion is illegal." On Tuesday, the family members reached the residence of BJP leader and MLA Mausam Chaudhary and sought help. The MLA's husband, Aishwarya Mausam Chaudhary, assured them of help. He said, "The investigation will reveal whether the minor converted under coercion, temptation, or any pressure. The priority is to bring the minor safely back home." He said - he got information about this matter only yesterday. He contacted some people from Bijnor working in Jammu and Kashmir. Currently, a police team has gone to Jammu and Kashmir and the child is expected to reach Bijnor soon. CO City Sangram Singh said- A case has been registered in the matter. Further action will be taken once the boy reaches Bijnor.

stories.title: BHU exam question sparks fresh academic controversy:Debate grows over ‘Brahmanical Patriarchy’ reference in MA History semester paper
stories.summary: A question on “Brahmanical Patriarchy” in a Banaras Hindu University semester examination has triggered sharp debate among academicians, teachers and historians. The question appeared in the MA History fourth semester paper titled Women in Modern Indian Society, conducted by the History Department under the Faculty of Social Sciences. The disputed question asked students to explain the meaning of “Brahmanical Patriarchy” and discuss how it allegedly hindered the progress of women in ancient India. Question triggers academic debate The three-hour examination carried a total of 70 marks and was divided into three sections. It included optional questions, short-answer questions and long-answer descriptive responses. Different opinions have emerged within academic circles over whether such terminology should be used in university examinations, especially in the present social climate. Senior academician and retired professor from Sociology Dept of BHU Dr A. K. Joshi commented that not only it creates confusion among students but such topics are dangerous for the society also as it has several other dimensions too. Professor calls term academically recognized Professor Anuradha Singh from the History Department said the phrase “Brahmanical Patriarchy” is an established academic term that became widely discussed during the 1990s. She noted that meanings of concepts and terminology evolve over time depending on social and historical contexts. Key points raised by the professor included: Ancient India cannot be viewed uniformly Professor Singh also argued that the condition of women in ancient India cannot be assessed through a single national lens. According to her, social structures differed across regions and historical periods, making broad conclusions problematic. She maintained that analysing one region or era and applying it universally to the entire country would not be academically appropriate. While Dr Joshi opined that distorted colonial interpretations should be removed and replaced with factual, balanced historical academic content. Other questions focused on women’s history The paper also included questions on women’s issues and historical institutions from different periods. Among the questions asked were: Students were also asked how colonial-era education helped Indian women bridge the divide between private and public life. University rejects controversy allegations Responding to the criticism, the university administration issued an official clarification stating that the question strictly followed the prescribed syllabus and was framed entirely in an academic context. The administration said attempts to create unnecessary controversy around the examination were inappropriate, reiterating that the question paper was prepared according to the approved curriculum of the course.

stories.title: Gorakhpur-Lucknow highway to become smart:High-tech surveillance at every kilometer; traffic jams accidents to be monitored
stories.summary: People traveling between Gorakhpur and Lucknow are going to get major relief soon. Considering the increasing traffic pressure, road accidents, and long traffic jam problems, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has started preparations to develop the Lucknow-Gorakhpur National Highway-27 as a smart highway. After the new system is implemented, there will be high-tech surveillance 24 hours throughout the entire route and the traffic system will be controlled with modern technology. Smart system to be installed on Gorakhpur-Lucknow route NHAI will install an Advanced Traffic Management System (ATMS) on the highway. Through this, every activity on the road will be monitored. Information about accidents, traffic jams, or over-speeding will immediately reach the control center, which will help speed up relief and rescue operations. Under the project, two main control centers and one sub-control center will be established. This will enable monitoring of the entire highway network from Gorakhpur to Lucknow simultaneously. Cameras at Every Kilometer To strengthen the security system, 238 CCTV and PTZ cameras will be installed on the highway. These cameras will be operated from the control room and can be rotated in any direction for surveillance when needed. Additional cameras will be installed at accident-prone areas, junctions, and interchanges. Besides this, Video Incident Detection Systems and ANPR cameras will be installed every 10 kilometers. As soon as vehicles overspeeding or breaking traffic rules are identified, the system will immediately send an alert. Every Update Available During Journey For the convenience of travelers, 18 digital display boards will be installed on the highway. These boards will show real-time information about weather, road conditions, traffic jams, and diversions. Additionally, 24 speed detection systems will be installed to monitor vehicle speeds. For the safety of people traveling on the highway, 122 emergency call boxes will also be installed. In case of vehicle breakdown, accident, or medical emergency, people will be able to directly seek help from the control room. According to NHAI officials, the objective of this smart highway project is to make travel from Gorakhpur to Lucknow safe, fast, and convenient. Keeping this in view, 52 special traffic equipment will be installed at diversion points. This will enable assessment of traffic pressure in advance and allow vehicles to be cleared in an organized manner, reducing the problem of long traffic jams.

stories.title: Woman found dead 4 days after engagement:Body discovered near Sushant Golf City; deceased left home for office but never returned
stories.summary: A case of murder of a girl has come to light in Lucknow, four days after her engagement. The girl had left home to go to the office but did not return. On Monday at 8 am, her body was found in the forest area of Sushant Golf City. Passersby noticed it and informed the police. There was panic in the area. In the police's preliminary investigation, it is suspected that the body was dumped after the murder. The police took possession of the body, sent it to the mortuary, and started identification. Meanwhile, when the family members reached the police station on Monday afternoon to file a missing person report, the police showed them a photograph of the body. The mother identified her daughter Shivani Singh (22) after seeing the photograph. The family members said, “Shivani's engagement had taken place four days ago, on May 14. She had left home at 10 am on May 17 (Sunday) but did not return by night. We got worried and started searching. When nothing was found anywhere, we went to the police. They told us about a body being found. When we saw the photograph, the ground slipped from under our feet.” See pictures Engagement took place on May 14, preparations were underway at home Shivani lived in a rented house in Eldeco Garden, Raksha Block with her parents and 19-year-old younger sister. The family's financial condition is weak. Mother Geeta (39) does sweeping and mopping work in houses, while father Deepu (42) does shuttering work. According to family members, Shivani got engaged to a boy named Prakash on May 14. The family was busy with wedding preparations. She had left home saying she was going to office Deceased Shivani's mother Geeta Singh said that her daughter worked in a real estate company office. On Sunday, she had left home saying she was going to office. When she didn't return till late night, family members started searching. Later when they reached the police, they got the news of her death. Police investigating CCTV and call details DCP South Amit Kumar Anand said- After the body was identified, the case is being investigated seriously. Police are gathering clues based on the girl's call details, CCTV footage around home and office, and last location. The reason behind the murder is not clear yet. Police will solve the case soon.

stories.title: Cobra troubled by heat, coils around ice bottle:Cooling pads installed at Kanpur Zoo to protect snakes from heat stroke
stories.summary: Today the city's temperature remained around 43.2C. Now the effect of heat has started showing on the reptiles of Kanpur Zoo as well. Cold-blooded creatures like snakes and iguanas are also troubled by this scorching heat. To protect snakes from this heat, Kanpur Zoo administration has come up with a unique and indigenous solution. Here, for the first time, ice bottles have been arranged in the snake enclosures. The snakes and iguanas living in the enclosures are now sitting on the bottles and taking ice massage. See these 3 pictures Snakes become disturbed at temperatures above 37 degrees Zoo wildlife veterinarian Dr. Nasir explained that reptile class creatures (such as snakes, lizards, crocodiles) are extremely sensitive to temperature. They are called 'cold blooded' or in scientific language 'Poikilotherm' animals. This means that their bodies do not have sweat glands and they can only change their body temperature according to the environment up to a certain limit. If the enclosure temperature falls below 24 degrees Celsius, their digestive system gets disrupted. On the other hand, if the temperature crosses 37 to 40 degrees, they face the risk of heat stroke. Excessive heat causes burn-like marks to appear on snakes' bodies and can even lead to their death. 'Cooling Pad' made from deep freezer ice and jute sacks To protect snakes from heat stroke, Kanpur Zoo, under the direction of Zoo Director Kanhaiya Patel, is filling plastic bottles with water and freezing them in deep freezers. After this, jute sacks are wrapped over these frozen bottles and sewn shut. This keeps the ice frozen in the bottles for a long time. These bottles are being placed in snake resting areas and water tanks. When it gets hot, snakes cling to these sacks. Doctors say this arrangement is working as an alternative to 'sandalwood trees' for snakes. Additionally, jute sacks are also being wrapped around tree branches in the enclosures and water is being sprayed on them. 50 snakes of 8 species, iguanas being served cucumber-watermelon According to Dr. Nasir, there are currently about 50 snakes of 8 species in Kanpur Zoo. Among the venomous snakes are cobras and Russell's vipers, while the non-venomous ones include rock pythons, sand boas, common trinket snakes and water snakes. There is also a 'reticulated python' found in South-East Asia. These snakes are being fed white mice in their diet. The herbivorous creature 'Iguana' found in the Amazon forests of America is also a center of attraction, of which there are four in number. To protect the iguanas from heat, ice bottles have also been placed in their enclosure. Along with this, taking special care of their diet, juicy items like watermelon, papaya, cucumber and gherkin are being given so that there is no water deficiency in their body. Water spray being done to prevent the slough from drying During the summer season, the snakes' slough starts drying up and comes off in pieces, which causes them considerable discomfort. To prevent this, wildlife staff are spraying light water mist (sprinkle) on their bodies. Additionally, the pools (tanks) in the enclosures are always being filled with cold water so that the snakes can swim in them whenever they want to regulate their body temperature.

stories.title: Terms of 57,000 Pradhans in UP expire on May 26:Administrative committee to take charge; dept sends proposal to Cabinet
stories.summary: The term of 57,695 Gram Pradhans in Uttar Pradesh will end on May 26, but there is still no clarity on when Panchayat elections will be held in the state. Due to this, the Panchayati Raj Department has sent a proposal to the Cabinet to appoint administrators or form administrative committees to manage Gram Panchayats after the current Pradhans complete their term. The proposal is likely to get approval within the next few days. Earlier, around two months ago, Panchayati Raj Minister Omprakash Rajbhar had told Bhaskar in an interview that Panchayat elections in the state could be held by July 12. Pradhan Sangh demands formation of 'Administrative Committee' National President of Rashtriya Panchayati Raj Gram Pradhan Sangathan, Akhilesh Singh, says that a delegation from the organisation met CM Yogi Adityanath on April 20 and demanded the formation of an administrative committee. Subsequently, on May 16, the same demand was put forward during a meeting with BJP State President Pankaj Chaudhary. Meanwhile, the organisation's Vice President, Lalit Kumar Sharma, explains that if panchayat elections are not held on time, the state government or the District Magistrate can form an administrator or an administrative committee under sub-section 3A of Section 12 of the Panchayati Raj Act 1947. The administrative committee includes the Gram Pradhan or a chairman designated by the government. Additionally, ward members of the panchayat, including the Gram Pradhan, and Gram Panchayat assistants, are appointed as members. Practical difficulties arise when an administrator is appointed Akhilesh Singh, National President of the Pradhan Sangathan Sangh, states that appointing a government employee as an administrator in Gram Panchayats creates several practical problems for the villagers. Officials said that Gram Panchayat assistants will become administrators Amit Singh, Director of the Panchayati Raj Department, states that there is no provision to extend the tenure of Gram Pradhans. Administrators will be appointed at the government level. The official said that there is a provision to appoint 'Gram Panchayat Assistants' of the panchayats as 'Administrators'. Until elections are held, the administrator handles the work of the Gram Panchayat. 3 reasons for appointing an administrator 1. The final publication of the voter list for the Panchayat elections has not yet been done; the tenure of Gram Pradhans is till May 26, while the final publication of the list will be on June 10. 2. The proposal for the formation of an OBC Commission to determine OBC reservation in Panchayat elections has been approved by the Cabinet. The commission will submit its report within three to six months of its formation. After that, the reservation for the elections will be determined. This may take six months. 3. The government is considering holding Panchayat elections after the Assembly elections. Political parties are also in principle agreement, but the matter is pending in the Allahabad High Court.

stories.title: Suvendu's PA murder case takes new turn:Accused Rajkumar hails from UP's Ballia, has criminal record; Bengal Police raid Ghazipur
stories.summary: The main shooter Rajkumar Singh, arrested in the murder of Chandranath Rath, PA to West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, had previously been jailed in an assault case. A case under the SC/ST Act is ongoing against him. Currently, he was out on bail. During the investigation, a photo of shooter Rajkumar with Bhojpuri actor Pawan Singh also surfaced, in which he is seen standing with Pawan in a green T-shirt. Rajkumar, a resident of Rasra, Ballia, was apprehended by the CBI from Muzaffarnagar on Monday. Earlier, on May 10, Raj Singh, also a resident of Ballia, was apprehended from Ayodhya. Meanwhile, West Bengal police also raided Ghazipur last night. The police had come to apprehend Sanjay Rai and Vinay Rai in the PA Chandranath Rath murder case. Both their houses were searched, but no clue was found. After this, the police picked up Aman, Sanjay Rai's nephew. He was released at night after a long interrogation. Two days after the Bengal election results were announced, 42-year-old Chandranath Rath was shot dead on May 6. The attackers stopped his car and fired several rounds. Chandranath Rath was hit by 3 bullets in the chest and abdomen. Due to the seriousness of the matter, the investigation was handed over to the CBI. Rajkumar was apprehended near the toll plaza while returning from Haridwar This is the house of Rajkumar, a resident of Ratopur village in Ballia district. Silence has spread here after his arrest. CBI already knew about Rajkumar's activities. Information was received that he was returning from Haridwar. Following this, the CBI team laid a trap near the toll plaza located in the Chhapar area of Muzaffarnagar. Early Monday morning, as soon as Rajkumar's car reached near the toll, the CBI team apprehended him. After this, he was interrogated for a long time. 24-hour remand granted by the court CBI CO Rajesh Kumar presented Rajkumar in the CJM court, from where he was granted a 24-hour remand. Now, CBI is interrogating him to uncover the murder conspiracy and other people involved in it. Additionally, he will be questioned about his links with Raj Singh, also a resident of Ballia. Rajkumar was preparing to go abroad Tribhuvan Narayan Singh, a resident of Rattopur village in Ballia, used to work for LT in Ayodhya. He has been at home since retiring in March. He has 2 sons and one daughter. The daughter is the eldest. The youngest son studies in class 5. Rajkumar Singh is Tribhuvan's elder son. He studied up to BA first year. He dropped out of studies because he wasn't interested. After that, he started working as a crane helper in Mumbai. However, he quit his job 8 months ago and came home. Rajkumar was preparing to go abroad for work after getting his passport made. For this, he had applied for his character certificate. When the certificate was not issued due to a lawsuit, he went to the High Court. About 3 years ago, he had been jailed after his name came up in a dispute with people from the Harijan community in Rattopur village, Ballia. Father said - We have no relatives in West Bengal Accused Rajkumar Singh's father, Tribhuvan Narayan Singh, said - Today morning around 6:45 AM, some CBI officials from Muzaffarnagar called. They asked, "Are you Tribhuvan Narayan Singh?" I said, "Yes." After that, they asked, "Is Rajkumar Singh your son?" I again replied in the affirmative. It was stated from that side that we took him into custody from here. They were mentioning some case from 2026. After that, what they were saying, we did not understand. They informed that the PA of CM Suvendu Adhikari was murdered in West Bengal, and he is being interrogated in the same case. Where Rajkumar was on the 6th-7th, even we don't know. He came here on May 10, 11, or 12. He had told his mother that he was going out. Today, the police did not come to our place, but yesterday, people in civil dress came in two vehicles. They were inquiring about Rajkumar. They had asked, 'Where is he?' They took our mobile phone and also took Rajkumar's photo with them. We have no relatives in West Bengal. Whether he went to Bengal or not, I don't know. CBI is investigating. The truth will be revealed. Whatever the truth is, it will come out. The first accused, Raj Singh, was caught on May 10 Raj Singh, a resident of Ballia, was arrested from Ayodhya on May 10 in the murder of PA Chandranath Rath. After this, he was sent to 13-day police custody by the court. After his arrest, a poster of Raj Singh had surfaced. In it, he has identified himself as the State General Secretary of Akhil Bharatiya Kshatriya Mahasabha. His Facebook account has a picture with Minister Dayashankar Singh. He also has a reel with former MP Brijbhushan Singh. According to neighbors, Raj wanted to become a politician. He was preparing to contest the Block Pramukh election. Suspicion of 8 people involved in the murder Investigating agencies believe that at least 8 people were involved in the conspiracy and execution of the murder. These people had reconnoitered for several days before killing PA Chandranath Rath. The attackers' car had passed through Bali Toll Plaza before the murder. Here, a person in the car had made the toll payment via UPI. Through the mobile number linked to this digital transaction, the police identified one accused. Then they reached the rest of the accused. Meanwhile, after the initial investigation, the Bengal Police had expressed apprehension about the involvement of contract killers in the murder of Chandranath Rath. Police had said that Rath's murder was planned. Professional shooters might be involved in it. Police had seized a car from the crime scene, which was used to chase Rath's Scorpio. The car's number plate turned out to be fake. The car's chassis and engine numbers were erased. Additionally, two bikes were involved in the attack. One of these bikes was also found near a tea shop about 4 km from the crime scene. It also had a fake registration. Chandranath was with Suvendu since he was in TMC Chandranath was previously an officer in the Air Force. After taking VRS, he worked in the corporate sector for some time. After this, he entered politics. Chandranath had been working for Suvendu since he was in the Trinamool Congress. He was considered among Suvendu Adhikari's closest associates. Chandranath became part of Suvendu's official team in 2019, when Suvendu was a minister in the Mamata Banerjee government. Chandranath took charge of Suvendu's election campaign in Bhawanipur. Bhawanipur is the same seat from where Suvendu defeated Mamata Banerjee in the assembly elections by about 15,000 votes. Chandranath's mother also joined BJP with Suvendu Like Suvendu, Chandranath's family was also previously associated with TMC. His mother, Hashi Rath, held a position in the local panchayat body in Purba Medinipur during TMC rule, but joined the BJP with Suvendu Adhikari in 2020. Chandranath was of a calm nature and low-profile. He completed his studies from Rahara Ramakrishna Mission. Despite being close to Suvendu for many years, he always stayed away from the limelight. Chandrakant does not have any photo with Suvendu. Understand the entire incident with a 90-minute timeline Chandranath left Kolkata around 9 PM: Chandranath was returning from Kolkata in a Scorpio to his rented house in Madhyamgram. The driver was driving the car. Chandranath was sitting next to him. Scorpio seen in CCTV at 10 PM Around 9:58 PM, Chandranath's Scorpio was seen passing on the road in a CCTV camera in Madhyamgram, about 20 kilometers from Kolkata. A little while after the Scorpio passed, a car and three people on two bikes were seen following it from the area. 10:30 AM: Car blocked the Scorpio's path Near Doharia Junction in Madhyamgram, the car overtook the Scorpio and stopped in front of it. The Scorpio driver had to stop the car. Assailant on bike started firing Before Chandranath and his driver could understand anything, the bike-borne assailants came from the left and fired 6 to 10 rounds. Criminals fled leaving the car After committing the crime, the criminals left the car there and fled on motorcycles via two different routes. Car's number plate fake Police seized the car from the crime scene, but when the number was checked, it turned out to be fake. The car's chassis number had also been tampered with. Glock 47X Pistol Used in Murder The attackers had used a Glock 47X pistol. Ordinary criminals do not use such modern weapons. The way the attack happened, only a professional shooter could have carried it out.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi warns of tough economic phase ahead:Says PM Modi left for foreign tour instead of handling situation
stories.summary: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi is on a two-day visit to Uttar Pradesh. Speaking in Rae Bareli on Tuesday, he said an economic storm is about to hit the country. He alleged that the economic structure created by Prime Minister Narendra Modi for Adani and Ambani will not survive and will completely collapse. He added that ordinary people will suffer the most because of it. Rahul reached Lucknow Airport from Delhi at around 11.30 am on Tuesday. UP Congress chief Ajay Rai and Rajya Sabha MP Pramod Tiwari welcomed him at the airport. Hundreds of Congress workers and supporters arrived with banners and posters and raised slogans in his support. From Lucknow, Rahul left for Rae Bareli by road. On the way, he stopped his convoy and visited the Churuwa Temple to offer prayers to Lord Hanuman. The temple priest welcomed him with a garland and offered prasad. Later, he inaugurated a marriage hall built through MP funds in Bachhrawan and interacted with local villagers. Rahul Gandhi will stay in Rae Bareli on Tuesday. He will address a small public gathering in Khiro village and attend a women’s interaction programme in Lalganj. On May 20, he will meet people during a public interaction programme and unveil the statue of freedom fighter Veera Pasi. After that, he will leave for Amethi. Since the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Rahul Gandhi has visited Rae Bareli six times. This is his seventh visit. Earlier, he had visited the constituency on January 19, 2026. Political analysts believe Rahul has already started preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections.

stories.summary: A week before Bakrid in UP, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath issued a strict warning against offering prayers on roads. stories.title: IMD issues heatwave warning for 39 UP districts:Banda hottest in the country with 47.6°C; schools closed in Varanasi, Agra
stories.summary: Severe heat and heatwave continue to prevail in UP. The mercury has crossed 47 °C. Banda remained the hottest city in the country for the second consecutive day. The maximum temperature was recorded at 47.6 °C. Since Tuesday morning, people in all districts have been suffering due to the intense sunlight. Loo-like winds are blowing. The Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a heatwave alert for 39 districts today, including Prayagraj, Kanpur, and Varanasi. IMD states that severe heat will prevail across the entire state for 3 days starting today. Most districts will be affected by the heatwave. During the day, temperatures will cross 45 °C. In such a situation, people should not step out of their homes during the day. Take special care of children, the elderly, and sick people. Meanwhile, due to the severe heat, all schools in Kashi have been closed until May 25. A holiday has been declared today (May 19) in Agra and Chitrakoot. Water is being sprinkled on the roads in Kanpur. Lucknow's meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said- The weather in the state will remain dry. Severe heat will prevail till May 23. Temperatures will rise in most parts of the state. Heatwave will occur. Temperatures may increase by 3 to 4C. Meanwhile, the monsoon may reach Kerala around May 26. It is estimated that the monsoon will enter UP via Gorakhpur on June 18. However, this is a tentative date. Heatwave alert in these cities How will the weather be for the next 5 days?

stories.title: Mayawati sent police after him, flew with Mulayam in helicopter:Once a powerful strongman in Purvanchal, now Vijay Mishra's entire family in jail
stories.summary: Once known as one of the most powerful strongmen in Purvanchal politics, Vijay Mishra’s entire family is now behind bars. On May 15, the MP/MLA Court sentenced his wife Ramkali Mishra and daughter-in-law Roopa Mishra. Ramkali and Roopa were sent to Gyanpur Jail. Vijay Mishra is already lodged in Agra Jail, while his son Vishnu Mishra is in Lakhimpur Jail. There was a time when Bhadohi was identified with Vijay Mishra’s name. His influence in eastern Uttar Pradesh was so strong that he remained an MLA for nearly two decades. Political parties relied on his support during elections, and senior leaders considered him important in the caste equations of the region. Today, however, his political empire has collapsed. How Vijay Mishra entered state politics Vijay Mishra’s rise in politics began in the 1980s. At that time, Bhadohi was part of the Varanasi district. Former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Kamalapati Tripathi wanted a strong Brahmin face in the area. Vijay Mishra, who was involved in the truck and petrol pump business, was approached to enter politics. Initially, he refused because he wanted to focus on business, but later agreed after repeated requests. Soon after entering politics, Vijay started gaining influence among Brahmins in the region. During a Block Pramukh election in Digh, celebrations after the victory of Abhay Raj Singh, who was linked to strongman Udaybhan Singh alias Doctor, reportedly included abusive remarks against Brahmins. Many people in the community then began seeing Vijay Mishra as someone who could challenge the existing power structure. Rise of influence in Purvanchal region In the 1990s, Vijay contested the Block Pramukh election. He spent heavily and reportedly ensured victory by getting all BDC candidates picked up before the election, allowing him to win unopposed. This victory increased his political ambitions. After Bhadohi became a district in 1994, Vijay strengthened his network and moved closer to Samajwadi Party chief Mulayam Singh Yadav. At that time, Shivkaran Yadav alias Kake was District Panchayat President and often criticised Mulayam Singh. Mulayam took a political gamble on Vijay Mishra and distributed tickets for three District Panchayat seats according to his recommendations. Vijay not only helped the party win those seats but also played a major role in getting the District Panchayat President elected from the Samajwadi Party. Mulayam trusted Vijay during the crucial elections In 2002, Vijay Mishra sought a ticket to contest the Assembly election from Gyanpur. Mulayam Singh reportedly put a condition before him he would get the ticket only if he also ensured victory for Mahesh Narayan Singh in Handia and Kailash Chaurasia in Mirzapur. Vijay agreed. In the election, he defeated BJP candidate Gorakhnath Pandey by 7,652 votes. The other two candidates also won. However, the election saw a major controversy. During polling, Gorakhnath Pandey’s brother Rameshwar Pandey was shot dead at a booth. The attackers had allegedly targeted Gorakhnath Pandey, but Rameshwar was travelling in the car that was attacked. Vijay Mishra’s name came up in the case, but the court later acquitted him due to lack of evidence. The investigation was later reopened by the Human Rights Commission and is still pending. Stories of power and political style As Vijay’s political influence grew, so did stories about his style and power. During rallies, he reportedly gifted gold chains instead of flower garlands to political leaders, with the size of the chain depending on the leader’s importance. Though he used a simple keypad phone, people close to him claimed he remembered more than 1,500 phone numbers without saving them. Vijay also maintained close relations with journalists in the region. It is said he arranged expensive Gucchi vegetable dishes for them, which were sometimes cooked by him or his wife Ramkali. People who skipped his events reportedly received calls warning them about a “penalty” for not attending. A religious image strengthened local political influence By 2007-08, Vijay Mishra had become an established Brahmin leader in Purvanchal. During Navratri, he observed nine-day fasts and organised large religious events. Eleven priests continuously chanted prayers at his residence, and thousands attended the final Havan ceremony. Reports say nearly 40,000 people came to offer oblations. Priests were gifted money, grains and cows. The same period also saw growing tension between Vijay Mishra and BSP chief Mayawati. In 2007, BSP formed a majority government in Uttar Pradesh. During preparations for the 2009 Bhadohi by-election, party leaders reportedly advised Mayawati that Vijay’s support was necessary to win. Mayawati allegedly offered him a place in BSP, but Vijay refused to leave Mulayam Singh. Mayawati failed to bring Vijay into the BSP By then, around 40 criminal cases had already been registered against him. Police pressure increased. During one campaign rally, Vijay reportedly appealed to Mulayam Singh for protection. Mulayam then famously declared that nobody could arrest Vijay Mishra while he was present. Vijay later flew away with Mulayam in a helicopter while the police watched. Vijay Mishra’s name later surfaced in several major criminal cases. One of the biggest involved the kidnapping and murder of coal businessman and Vishwa Hindu Parishad national treasurer Nand Kishore Rungta. A ransom of ₹2 crore was demanded after his abduction from Varanasi. When the money was not paid, he was killed. Vijay Mishra and Mukhtar Ansari were named in the case, but both were acquitted by the CBI court due to insufficient evidence. Criminal cases started damaging the political career From 1995 to 2010, Vijay reportedly controlled mining contracts across a large area. It was said that nobody else could secure contracts within a 20-kilometre stretch. His trucks allegedly moved without paying tolls. A major setback came in 2010 after a bomb attack on BSP minister Nand Gopal Gupta ‘Nandi’ outside a temple. The blast killed journalist Vijay Pratap Singh, Rakesh Malviya and the minister’s gunman. Nandi was critically injured. Vijay Mishra and others were accused in the case. While some accused were arrested, Vijay absconded and reportedly moved around Karnataka, Kolkata and Mumbai disguised as a sadhu. He was finally arrested by STF from Delhi in February 2011. Won the election despite staying in jail Even from jail, Vijay remained politically strong. In the 2012 Assembly election, Mulayam Singh again gave him a ticket. His wife and daughters campaigned for him, and he won by over 37,000 votes. But his political decline began after 2017 when Akhilesh Yadav denied him a ticket. Vijay publicly questioned why he had earlier been given party tickets if he was considered a strongman. He later contested on a Nishad Party ticket and won again, defeating BJP candidate Mahendra Bind. However, he was later removed from the party. The property dispute became a turning point later In 2020, relative Krishna Mohan Tiwari accused Vijay Mishra of illegally occupying property worth around ₹1500 crore, including land and buildings. Vijay was arrested from Madhya Pradesh on August 14, 2020, and has remained in jail since then. On May 15 this year, the MP/MLA Court sentenced Vijay Mishra, his wife Ramkali and son Vishnu to 10 years in jail in this case, while daughter-in-law Roopa Mishra received a four-year sentence. Just two days earlier, Vijay had been sentenced to life imprisonment in a 1980 murder case related to the killing of Prakash Narayan Pandey inside the court premises. He was also sentenced to 15 years in jail in a rape case filed by a folk singer from Varanasi. Once-feared leader is now completely politically isolated Apart from this, Vijay Mishra has twice been convicted under the Arms Act. Courts in Bhadohi and Prayagraj sentenced him to prison terms and imposed fines. Today, most of Vijay Mishra’s illegal properties in Prayagraj and Bhadohi have been demolished. Several pending cases are moving quickly through courts. The politician for whom parties once competed is now politically isolated, and even former allies avoid taking his name publicly.

stories.title: SP faces backlash after controversial Brahmin-prostitute comment:BJP takes frontfoot, Mayawati signals outreach to 12% vote bank
stories.summary: Date May 5. Jawahar Bhawan in Delhi. It was the launch event of a book titled 'Viruses of Caste and Communalism'. SP's national spokesperson Rajkumar Bhati made a comment about Brahmins. He said - 'Neither a Brahmin is good, nor a prostitute is good...'. A controversy was bound to erupt over his statement, and that's exactly what happened. BJP, which was recently embroiled in issues like the 'Choti Kand' (braid incident) and the insult to Shankaracharya, suddenly got a chance to make a comeback. From BJP's state president Pankaj Chaudhary to Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak, everyone started trying to prove SP as anti-Brahmin and anti-Hindu. SP's own Brahmin leaders are also upset with this statement. Congress state president Ajay Rai also targeted SP on this issue. BSP supremo Mayawati declared both BJP and SP as anti-Brahmin. She said - 'The real respect and security for Brahmins is only in BSP.' Read how political narratives are changing for the 12% vote bank First, watch the VIDEO BJP said - SP's mentality is 'divide and rule' On the controversial statement of the SP spokesperson, BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary said - This statement is not just of one person. This is proof of SP's 'DNA' and the corrupt mentality of 'divide and rule'. Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak said - Rajkumar Bhati's comment shows SP's mentality. He said - The Brahmin community gave direction to the country in terms of knowledge, culture, constitution and nation building. Such language for them is unfortunate. SP leader Azam Khan had called Bharat Mata a witch. Swami Prasad Maurya had burnt Ramcharitmanas. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav should apologise for this. Mayawati said- Brahmins are respected only in BSP Alankar Agnihotri, who has formed a party named 'Rashtriya Adhikar Morcha', staged a protest outside the SP office on May 12. He demanded the immediate dismissal of Rajkumar Bhati from the party. Alankar Agnihotri had resigned from his PCS officer post over the insult to Shankaracharya. UP Congress President Ajay Rai also demanded action against Rajkumar Bhati. On May 12, he wrote in an X post- There can be ideological differences in politics, but insulting an entire community is not right. An apology alone will not suffice. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav will have to take action against such leaders. BSP chief Mayawati called Rajkumar Bhati's statement indecent. In an X post on May 15, she said- The statement of the SP spokesperson hurt the Brahmin community. The SP chief should take cognizance. He should apologize to the Brahmin community. SP first angered Dalits, extremely backward classes, and the Muslim community. Now it is targeting Brahmins. FIR in Ghaziabad, Brahmin community issued warning BJP leader Dr. Ajay Sharma lodged an FIR at Kavinagar police station in Ghaziabad regarding Bhati's statement. Organizations associated with the Brahmin community are protesting in different parts of the state, including Dadri. Bhati's effigy was burnt in many places. Parshuram Sena condemned this statement by calling a Mahapanchayat. Deepak Pandit of Karni Sena called Bhati to protest. Then, he made the audio of the entire conversation viral. Several organizations warned that the Brahmin community would give a fitting reply to SP in the 2027 elections. SP would not even get 27 seats. Brahmin community is looking for an option According to senior journalist Yogesh Mishra, Brahmins voted for Congress for a long time. Then, they joined BJP due to the Ram Mandir issue. Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Syama Prasad Mookerjee played a crucial role in this. Now, OBC politics is happening in BJP. The 'Choti Kand' (braid incident) and the insult to Shankaracharya happened. This has disappointed Brahmins. The Brahmin community is looking for an option. An option that can come to power and whose credit goes to Brahmins. SP certainly seemed to be becoming an option for Brahmins. But, after the strengthening of PDA and the success achieved in the Lok Sabha, it seems that SP does not need Brahmins. SP's Brahmin leaders are enraged, Akhilesh still calm SP's Brahmin leaders have protested against Bhati's statement. MLA Amitabh Bajpai from Aryanagar in Kanpur said- Bhati's statement is unfortunate, condemnable, and inexcusable. An apology alone will not suffice. They will meet the SP chief and demand action. Pawan Pandey, who has been a minister in the SP government, said that such abusive language against the Brahmin community is unacceptable. Strict disciplinary action should be taken. Former SP MLA Santosh Pandey said that Bhati's mental balance is not stable. However, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav did not give any reaction. SP chief should clarify his stand Senior journalist Akhilesh Vajpayee says - BJP was on the back foot on the issue of beating young Brahmins by pulling their topknots in Magh Mela and the Shankaracharya insult. The Brahmin community was also angry about this. SP had then openly cornered BJP. To avoid this, BJP made SP rebel Dr. Manoj Pandey a minister in the UP cabinet. SP spokesperson Bhati's statement came at a time when BJP, after a massive victory in Bengal and Assam, has shifted its focus to UP. In this matter, the SP chief should clear his confusion. Akhilesh Yadav sometimes tries to show himself as a Hindu, and sometimes wears a cap to portray himself as pro-Muslim. How big a game-changer are Brahmins in UP? The Brahmin vote bank in UP is around 10-12%. The Brahmin community determines the winning and losing margin on 17 Lok Sabha seats and more than 100 Assembly seats. In Purvanchal, the Brahmin population on some seats in Gorakhpur, Deoria, Jaunpur, Bhadohi, Varanasi, Basti, Balrampur is between 15% to 20%. Brahmins dominate the rural areas of Kanpur Nagar, Kanpur Dehat, Unnao, Lucknow, Prayagraj in Central UP. After Muslims and Jatavs, Brahmins are a large vote bank in the state. Whichever party the Brahmins collectively supported, that party formed the government in the state. Since 2014, the Brahmin vote has been going to BJP, but the party is now targeting the OBC vote bank. To a large extent, the party has brought Thakurs to its side. Brahmins are looking for new options. According to experts, in the 2027 assembly elections, Brahmins will collectively support at the last moment whoever is in a position to change the government. Or they will support Brahmin candidates through tactical voting, even if they are contesting from different parties.

stories.title: CM Yogi orders 50% cut in ministers’ convoy vehicles:Big companies to follow 2-day work from home; Govt meetings to be held online
stories.summary: Following Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s appeal on fuel conservation and energy saving, the Uttar Pradesh government on Tuesday announced several major decisions. CM Yogi Adityanath said the number of vehicles in the convoys of the ministers and senior officials would be reduced by 50 percent with immediate effect. He also directed that ministers, MPs and MLAs should use public transport at least one day every week. Govt meetings and seminars to shift online The state government has decided that all official meetings, seminars, conferences and workshops will now be conducted virtually. Fifty percent of meetings in the state secretariat will also be held online. CM Yogi further appealed to citizens to observe a “No Vehicle Day” once every week. Advisory for work-from-home in industries and startups The Chief Minister said industrial establishments, major startups and other large organisations should be encouraged to adopt work-from-home arrangements. He directed officials to issue a state-level advisory recommending work from home for two days a week in offices and institutions employing large numbers of people. CM says everyone must support PM’s appeal During the meeting, CM Yogi said the world was currently witnessing instability and that people must act cautiously. He said the Prime Minister’s appeal should be followed seriously and added that government employees, school and college students, and different sections of society should all be connected to the campaign. High-level meeting held in Lucknow CM Yogi chaired the high-level meeting with officials at his residence in Lucknow on Tuesday evening. He instructed officers that the Centre’s appeal should not remain limited to paperwork and must be implemented strictly at the ground level. Additional Chief Secretaries (ACS) and Principal Secretaries from all major departments attended the meeting. The meeting took place just one day after PM Modi’s public appeal. PM Modi appealed for reduced fuel use amid global crisis Amid the energy crisis and economic challenges arising from the Iran-Israel conflict, PM Modi on May 10 and 11 urged people to use petrol, diesel and cooking gas in moderation. He also appealed to citizens to reduce unnecessary foreign travel, avoid excessive gold purchases and promote work-from-home practices. PM Modi repeats appeal on two consecutive days Addressing public events on May 10 and 11, PM Modi said the country must reduce petrol, diesel and gas consumption because global fuel prices had sharply increased due to the ongoing conflict in the region. He said India was more vulnerable to the crisis because it does not possess large oil reserves. The Prime Minister stressed the need for measures such as work from home and greater use of metro services in cities. He also referred to past wartime sacrifices, saying people earlier used to donate gold during national crises. He clarified that no donations were being sought now, but appealed to citizens not to buy gold for one year in order to save foreign exchange. PM Modi’s 5 major appeals Avoid buying gold for one year- PM Modi said a large amount of foreign exchange is spent on gold imports and appealed to people not to buy or donate gold for one year in the national interest. Save petrol and diesel, encourage carpooling- He urged people to reduce unnecessary use of vehicles, use metros and public transport, and adopt carpooling wherever possible. Reduce edible oil consumption- The Prime Minister said if every household reduced cooking oil consumption slightly, it would save foreign exchange and also benefit public health. Shift towards natural farming- He appealed for reduced dependence on chemical fertilisers and encouraged farmers to move towards natural farming practices. Postpone foreign travel- PM Modi also requested people to postpone foreign travel for weddings, holidays and other non-essential reasons due to rising economic pressure linked to global conditions and fuel costs. Opposition questions PM’s appeal Several opposition leaders criticised the Prime Minister’s remarks and demanded concrete relief measures instead of public appeals. Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi said running the country was “no longer within the Prime Minister’s control”. In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi wrote that PM Modi’s statements were ‘not sermons, but evidence of failure’. He said the public was now being told what to buy, what not to buy, where to travel and where not to travel after 12 years of governance. Akhilesh Yadav says BJP failed on economy and foreign policy Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav alleged that the BJP government had failed to manage both the economy and foreign policy. He claimed the government remembered the “crisis” only after elections ended and said the “real crisis” facing the country was the BJP itself. Sanjay Singh questions timing of appeal AAP leader Sanjay Singh also criticised the Centre over the timing of the appeal. He alleged that the government had borne the burden on citizens only until elections in five states were over, and was now asking people to reduce fuel and gas consumption and avoid buying gold.
